findings.title: Styled components use bare template literals instead of the mandated (props: any) => css`` function form
findings.description: The spec's 'Emotion styled component conventions' section states: 'All styled components use the Styled.* namespace pattern' with the form `styled.div((props: any) => { const t: any = props.theme; return css`...`; })`. Both Styled.Wrapper (lines 92-96) and Styled.Chip (lines 98-106) use bare template literals (`styled.span`...``) instead. Neither accesses the theme, so there is no runtime breakage today, but the convention is prescriptive ('All styled components use...') and these two components are non-conforming. Future maintainers adding theme-dependent styles to either will need to restructure the component. Fix: convert both to the (props: any) => css`` function form.
findings.fix: Convert Styled.Wrapper and Styled.Chip to use `styled.span((props: any) => { const t: any = props.theme; return css`label: ...; ...`; })` per the mandated convention.

findings.title: Failed-state subtitle uses em dash instead of spec-specified copy
findings.description: Spec section 3 table row for Failed state specifies subtitle: "No credit was used -- open to retry." (double hyphen as written in the spec). The implementation renders: "No credit was used — open to retry." (em dash, Unicode U+2014). While the em dash is typographically correct English, this is a literal copy mismatch from the spec. All other subtitle strings match the spec exactly. The spec is the authoritative source for copy; the implementation must match it unless the discrepancy is explicitly approved.
findings.fix: Align the subtitle string with the spec. Either the implementation should use the em dash (if that was the design intent and the spec's double-hyphen was a markdown rendering artifact) or the spec should be amended. Surface to Jessica for a decision — do not silently accept either form.
